query: For protective coatings on zirconium-alloy nuclear-fuel cladding, what single intervention could improve resistance to high-temperature oxidation while retaining suitability for service? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, states the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a ceramic coating to zirconium-alloy nuclear-fuel cladding will improve its resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
generation.mechanism: The ceramic coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing the oxidation rate of the zirconium alloy.
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the ceramic coating may depend on its composition, thickness, and application method.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated zirconium-alloy nuclear-fuel cladding exhibits a higher oxidation rate than the uncoated baseline under high-temperature conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
